notes: Read all four units, full Trump-democracy context, all eighteen candidates and the review. Anchored every election claim to the 2024 U.S. election, preserved the Democratic characterization of Republican conduct, named U.S. democracy, freedoms, institutions and courts, and normalized the beacon metaphor while retaining its vital-role evaluation. Restored the importance assigned to presidential judicial appointments and the separate judgment that judges matter.

claims.claim_text: The 2024 U.S. election is characterized as deciding whether the next American generation will have more or fewer rights and freedoms than prior generations.
Democrats characterize Trump and Republicans as stripping Americans of freedoms they fought to secure.
Reproductive freedom is characterized as at stake in the 2024 U.S. election.
Freedom from hate is characterized as at stake in the 2024 U.S. election.
Freedom from fear is characterized as at stake in the 2024 U.S. election.
Freedom to control one's destiny is characterized as at stake in the 2024 U.S. election.
Democrats would continue mobilizing Americans across political lines to defend U.S. democracy.
Democrats would restore trust they consider essential in U.S. institutions.
Democrats would preserve what they consider America's vital worldwide role in exemplifying democracy.
Appointing judges is characterized as one of a U.S. president's most important duties.
U.S. judges are characterized as important because they can uphold or roll back basic rights.
U.S. judges can uphold basic rights.
U.S. judges can roll back basic rights.
U.S. judges hear cases deciding women's freedom over reproductive healthcare.
U.S. judges hear cases deciding Americans' voting freedom.
U.S. judges hear cases deciding workers' freedom to unionize and earn a family-supporting wage.
U.S. judges hear cases deciding children's freedom to breathe clean air and drink clean water.
U.S. judges hear cases deciding whether a U.S. president is above the law.
